scope: Every image currently registered in constants/qaFixtures.js.
governingRule: The earlier blanket 'approved' classification is NOT retained. Registration as a QA fixture is not evidence of ownership, consent, licence or evaluation authorization. Absent an authorization record, the only defensible disposition is pending_provenance.

summary.note: Zero fixtures are approved. Not one has a source owner, licence, or use record anywhere in the repository. Two carry editor metadata inconsistent with project-owned photography.

metadataEvidence.method: Direct JPEG APP-segment parsing. Values below are read from the files, not inferred.

findings.interpretation: A 2002 timestamp and Photoshop 7 (released 2002) are inconsistent with imagery captured for this project. Indicates a third-party image of unknown origin. This is an indication, not proof — EXIF is trivially editable.
Picasa was a consumer photo tool discontinued in 2016. Also inconsistent with project-owned capture. Same caveat: indicative, not conclusive.

metadataEvidence.absent: No fixture carries EXIF GPS, camera Make, camera Model, Artist, or Copyright tags. There is no embedded attribution to recover.

fixtures.notes: Privacy-clean and technically the strongest candidate: person wearing product, brand not visible, backlit, partial occlusion. Blocked solely on provenance.
Non-fashion control (a printed souvenir mug). Privacy-clean. The mug carries third-party insignia, which is incidental to its use as a non-fashion control but is another unresolved rights question.
Multi-item scene: bag, sunglasses, book. Requires relabelling as a detection case (INV-5). Composition is characteristic of stock lifestyle photography.

fixtures.exifState: exif_present — IFD0 Software/DateTime, XMP, 5632-byte Photoshop APP13. Strip required.
fixtures.notes: EXIF indicates a 2002 Photoshop 7 file. Almost certainly third-party. Privacy-clean once EXIF is stripped.

fixtures.notes: Excluded from every Build 4 manifest and derived dataset. Basis: undocumented provenance combined with an identifiable person in a private setting. Age, legal status and absence of permission are NOT asserted — none is verified. Escalated separately at docs/scanner-accuracy/phase0c-fixture-escalation.md. The production asset is untouched by Build 4.

ownerActionsToClear: For each fixture: identify the source owner and produce a licence, purchase record, or written internal-evaluation authorization.
For the three with identifiable faces: obtain a model release, or approve a masked derivative, or replace the fixture.
For qa_bottom_skirt: resolve provenance, then decide replacement or removal via the separate production-safe task.
Where provenance cannot be established, replace the fixture rather than re-approving it on the basis that it is already in the repository.
